newsitem.title: THAILAND: Incoming Thai finmin urges lower interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Incoming Thai finmin urges lower interest rates.

text.p: Thailand's incoming finance minister Amnuay Viravan said on Sunday he would support lowering interest rates as a way of helping investors and boosting confidence in Thailand's slowing economy.

Amnuay, who is being sworn in as deputy prime minister and finance minister later on Sunday, told reporters after arriving from a summit of southeast Asian leaders he would bring up the matter at the new government's first cabinet meeting on Monday.

"Reducing the interest rate will make the invstments more competitive," Amnuay said. "I will urge cooperation from the Bank of Thailand on the issue of reducing interest rates, and this will be discussed by the cabinet on Monday," he said.
Last week central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond urged banks to cut interest rates to encourage slowing business investment.
Several banks responded by cutting their minimum lending rate -- Thailand's prime rate -- by 25 basis points, effective on Monday. The rates will range between 13-13.25 percent following the cuts.
